title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-elena-garcia
summary: Personal scratchpad collecting commands run, error snippets, and hypotheses while debugging intermittent GPU OOMs and CUDA/driver mismatch errors on serving nodes.
content:
Context:
- Intermittent OOMs seen on dedicated pool nodes when serving large-context prompts (~8k tokens) across batch sizes 1-4. Mostly rtx-a5000 and a100 nodes. Happens more often on older driver images (nvidia-driver 470.x) but also observed once on 525.x after a kernel update.

Notes / timeline:
- 2024-03-12: First saw crash during canary run for model xform-large-8k. Pod restarted, OOM in dmesg.
- 2024-03-15: Rolled containers back to previous image -> reduced frequency but not full stop.
- 2024-03-20: Noticed one node with mixed CUDA toolkit libs installed (11.0 and 11.7) due to leftover conda env.

Commands I ran (useful outputs pasted below):
- nvidia-smi -a
  -> Shows driver Version: 470.199.02 on node-a, 525.85.12 on node-b. GPU memory usage spikes but baseline low.
- dmesg | grep -i oom
  -> "Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child" followed by stack trace showing libc allocation failure.
- docker logs <container> --tail 200
  -> Torch/cuda runtime prints: "CUDA error: out of memory" at generation loop. No clear single allocation (happens after ~200 tokens sometimes).
- python trace (wrapped with try/except printing torch.cuda.memory_summary()):
  -> Before crash: Allocated: 18.2 GiB, Cached: 2.1 GiB, Total GPU memory: 24.0 GiB (a5000).

Suspicious error snippets encountered:
- "CUDA runtime version (11070) does not match driver version (10010)" (seen in one node)
- "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch"
- "NCCL WARN: Unhandled system error" occasionally during multi-GPU batch tests
- "cuDNN initialization failed: CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED" after kernel upgrade on one node

Hypotheses:
1) Driver/toolkit mismatch: Some nodes have mixed CUDA runtime / driver combos; leftover conda envs or custom /usr/local/cuda symlinks are creating mismatches. When torch loads a different libcudart.so than driver expects, memory allocation can behave badly or NVML reports mismatch.
2) Memory fragmentation / caching behavior: Long-lived processes with many different sequence lengths + attention caches cause fragmentation leading to apparent OOM even though total < capacity. Batching increases peak because of KV cache growth per request.
3) Kernel bug / driver regression: Newer drivers (525.x) changed memory accounting and interaction with MIG on a100, causing edge OOMs under certain allocation patterns.
4) Host OOM / cgroups: Sometimes host swap or cgroups limit (docker memory) triggered kill and dmesg looked like GPU OOM. Need to verify host oom_score_adj and container memory limits.

Quick wins / fixes tried:
- Restarted nvidia-persistenced and container runtime on offending nodes -> temporarily reduced errors.
- Cleaned conda envs and removed stray /usr/local/cuda symlink; reinstalled correct libcuda symlinks to match driver 525.85.12.
- Set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 to reduce fragmentation (tested on a single instance). Observed fewer OOMs but not full resolution.
- Forced torch to use torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False for reproducibility (felt unrelated but kept for tests).
- Exported CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to isolate single GPU on heavy batches -> reduced chance of multi-GPU NCCL errors.

Repro steps (best attempt):
1) Use model checkpoint xform-large-8k, context 8k, batch_size 4, device a5000 with driver 470.199.02 and cuda toolkit 11.7 libs linked via conda.
2) Run load + repeated generate with variable lengths (1-2000 tokens). After ~50-200 requests, observe CUDA OOM in logs.
3) On failing container, run python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())' -> sometimes reports toolkit 11.7 while nvidia-smi shows driver 470.x -> mismatch.

Diagnostic commands to run next time (checklist):
- ssh node -> sudo nvidia-smi -q -d SUPPORTED_CLOCKS,DRIVER_MODEL,FB_MEMORY
- ldconfig -p | grep libcudart -> check which libcudart.so is symlinked in /usr/lib and container
- ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch.__file__)" ) | grep cuda -> see linked runtime libs used by torch inside container
- python -c 'import ctypes; print(ctypes.CDLL("libnvidia-ml.so.1").nvmlInit())' to check NVML init (wrap in try/except)
- strace -f -e open,read,write -p <pid> when crash happens to find which .so loaded just prior to OOM
- capture dmesg -T and journalctl -u docker (or containerd) around the time of crash

Longer-term mitigations to try:
- Standardize base runtime image: pin driver-aware libcuda versions and strip conda's /usr/local/cuda from production images. Add smoke test on startup to verify nvidia-smi driver/runtime match (fail fast).
- Add per-process memory fraction guard and graceful fallbacks: if memory usage > 85% then return degraded response or reduce generation length.
- Investigate switching to CUDA 12 driver runtime images on a staggered schedule after internal tests.
- Improve observability: record torch.cuda.memory_reserved/allocated per request token step to find allocation spike points.

Random notes / useful links:
- NCCL env vars to try: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 when debugging network-related NCCL errors.
- Try CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to make stack traces deterministic (slower).
- Known issue: "Driver/library version mismatch" often fixed by reinstalling nvidia driver or ensuring LD_LIBRARY_PATH preferred the driver's lib.
- GH PR: runtime/pull/987 has a small fix to remove /usr/local/cuda from ship image.

Next actions:
- Run the diagnostic checklist on node-a (the 470 driver one) next time the canary runs. Leave prepared commands in /tmp/gpu-debug-script.sh.
- Ask infra (Raja) to schedule driver upgrade window for pool nodes to unify 525.x across dedicated pool or roll back to a known-good 470.x + matching toolkit, depending on test results.
- Add a CI job that runs a quick torch + nvidia-smi consistency check inside built container images.

Quick paste of an error blob seen 2024-03-20:
"RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total capacity; 21.50 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 22.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/server/generate.py\", line 212, in handle_request
    out = model.generate(...)
  File \"/opt/conda/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py\", line 1614, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: unreported error
nvml: Driver/library version mismatch
"

Tone: scratchpad — choppy; saving so others can reproduce. Will merge findings into a Confluence post once we have deterministic repro or clear driver action.
